slice: Review the four-wave provider activation approach before any member-facing Crucible change.
sharedContext: Broad VPGMs currently treat Supabase account custody as the spine, Stripe Billing as a separate money lane, Stripe Identity/Plaid/Twilio as narrow dated checks, and Checkr as policy-blocked.
Every provider must have one job, one member surface, one minimal retained receipt, one deletion or expiry rule, one executable proof, and one stopping line.
Adapters and sandbox access are infrastructure, not finished member capabilities.
No production provider action, credential work, schema/RLS, spend, push, deploy, new task, subagent, or foreground input is authorized.
liveStrings: One member journey. Different tools for different jobs.
Keep one member connected to their work
Connect membership without turning payment into trust
Add only the check a conversation needs
Keep background screening blocked until the rules are ready
Only checks labeled available can be started. Test and sandbox activity is not live verification.
knownGaps: The member-stage list currently places Stripe Billing beside account creation while the activation roadmap puts owner-bound records before billing.
Readiness uses multiple compatible but potentially drifting vocabularies across the slot catalog and ledger.
Plaid sandbox access and scaffolding do not yet provide a complete Link-to-minimal-receipt-to-removal proof.
Twilio has an adapter contract but no provider route; Checkr is intentionally policy-blocked.
All M9 architecture and proof work is local and unpushed.

PETRA.vision: Judge whether the four-wave activation order is correctly scoped and whether it should become the canonical local release plan.
PETRA.pull: Inspect the current slot catalog, readiness ledger, data boundaries, and Crucible activation waves.
go: Return GO, PATCH, or NO_GO on the order: account custody, billing, narrow checks, policy-blocked screening.
Name any provider whose current state is overstated or internally contradictory.
Specify the smallest next source-bound proof that advances the stack without opening a human gate.
PETRA.momentum: Return a terminal scope ruling and stop.
PETRA.outOfLane: Review only; no code, provider action, legal approval, secret, schema/RLS, spend, push, deploy, new task, subagent, or gate approval.

ENDER.vision: Judge whether the four-wave member explanation clarifies the journey or reads like internal infrastructure homework.
ENDER.pull: Review the existing Crucible roadmap and proposed provider grouping.
go: Name the human question each wave must answer.
Cut insider language and vendor-first framing.
Return a bounded visual/copy recommendation without implementing it.
ENDER.outOfLane: No code, providers, secrets, spend, push, deploy, new task, subagent, or final creative approval.

BEAN.vision: Attack the activation plan for false readiness, privacy leakage, proof inflation, and provider-specific trust claims.
BEAN.pull: Review routes, adapters, slot states, retention boundaries, and hard gates.
go: Identify every place code-path-present could be mistaken for usable or live.
Attack Plaid amount privacy, Twilio possession claims, Stripe payment-versus-trust separation, and Checkr legal gating.
Return executable blockers or an explicit bounded pass.
BEAN.outOfLane: No code, provider action, legal approval, secrets, schema/RLS, spend, push, deploy, new task, or subagent.
